frequency_question: How often do established international technology transfer and co-production agreements for high-tech munitions successfully reach operational domestic assembly or manufacturing within a tight two-year window?
membership_rule: Includes official intergovernmental or industry agreements to produce advanced guided missiles (e.g., Patriots, Javelins, Storm Shadows, or similar tactical systems) domestically outside of the original manufacturer's primary facilities. Excludes simple maintenance depots or storage facilities that do not involve component manufacture or final assembly.

cases.name: Taiwan-US domestic production of Hsiung Feng and local Patriot maintenance/assembly initiatives
South Korea-Germany/US licensed production of Taurus KEPD 350 and Hyunmoo series components
Poland-Norway/US co-production initiatives for missile components under defense modernization
India-Russia BrahMos supersonic cruise missile joint venture domestic production line
Turkey-US/European licensed production of various guided munitions (SOM-J development phase)

coverage_note: 5 named major cases; representative of high-complexity defense technology transfers.
known_gaps: Classified or highly covert wartime domestic production efforts (e.g., non-publicized emergency facilities) are difficult to fully verify through standard historical datasets.
skeleton: Cases categorized by whether wartime urgency accelerated timelines versus standard bureaucratic defense procurement schedules.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 5 named historical defense technology localization attempts within the specified timeframe.
validity_reason: Global defense industrial base practices and technology transfer security protocols change slowly over multi-year cycles.
